updated_content: Earns interest on principal plus accumulated interest, growing exponentially over time according to A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt). The effective growth depends on whether the nominal rate accounts for inflation (real vs nominal return), how frequently interest compounds (daily, monthly, annually — higher frequency yields greater effective annual rate), and the investment horizon — exponential growth makes horizon the dominant factor, dwarfing rate differences over decades.

Includes the standard compound interest formula A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) for clarity. Reviewed and approved by human operator.
